question.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}={b}_{1}+{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}=-{b}_{1}?$
question.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}={b}_{1}+{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}=-{b}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. From the second equation, we get 

$$
{b}_{1}=-{c}_{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{c}_{1}=(-{c}_{2})+{b}_{2}\,⟹\,{b}_{2}={c}_{1}+{c}_{2}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-3{b}_{1}+4{b}_{2} \\  & =-3(-{c}_{2})+4({c}_{1}+{c}_{2}) \\  & =3{c}_{2}+4{c}_{1}+4{c}_{2} \\  & =4{c}_{1}+7{c}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 7\end{aligned}].$
